thread:
corey: quick question - we applied a TF change that adds an aws_kms_grant for IRSA pods, but pods still get AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt :thinking:
elaine: did you run `terraform apply` in the shared infra workspace or the app workspace?
corey: shared infra workspace. apply succeeded, shows aws_kms_grant resource created.
ben: are you using `aws_kms_key` + `aws_kms_grant` or relying on key policy? sometimes grants take a few seconds to propagate.
corey: using `aws_kms_grant` with `grantee_principal` referencing the IAM OIDC role ARN for svcacct. here's the terraform snippet I used:

```
resource \"aws_kms_grant\" \"irsa_grant\" {
  name            = \"irsa-vec-grant\"
  key_id          = aws_kms_key.app_data.key_id
  grantee_principal = \"arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/eksctl-my-cluster-NodeInstanceRole-xxxxx\"
  operations      = [\"Decrypt\",\"Encrypt\"]
}
```

sam: if the grantee is a role created by IRSA (federated principal), the ARN in the grant has to match the assumed role principal, not the k8s serviceaccount string. also make sure role trust policy allows sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.
alice: also check the pod's namespace/serviceaccount annotation timing — helm charts that create SA + annotation + deploy can have a race where the serviceaccount isn't annotated when the pod starts. we saw that with external-secrets.
corey: good point. I added the annotation via helm hook `post-install` but that may be too late.
deploy-bot: NOTICE: terraform apply completed at 2026-03-17T15:12:14Z for workspace infra-shared (run id: tf-run-4521)
ben: another thing — if you're using kms grants, ensure the KMS key policy doesn't block grants. key policy can include `grants` restrictions. run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <id>` from account to confirm.
corey: ran `aws kms list-grants`, shows the grant id. but still Decrypt denied.
elaine: check CloudTrail/CloudWatch logs for KMS denied -> will show which principal was rejected. Also check STS `get-caller-identity` from the pod to confirm principal ARN.
sam: temporary workaround: add the IAM principal directly to key policy so it's immediate; grants are supposed to be immediate but we've seen propagation lag in some regions.
alice: if you go for key policy patch, prefer to do it in infra code too and leave a comment. otherwise we get drift.
corey: thanks — I'll check pod identity and logs, and if still blocked, I'll patch key policy and open a small PR to revert later. pinging @ben for quick review if I go with key-policy change.
ben: ack, will review. :thumbsup:
